reason: The elbow joint should connect the arm bones and help make the elbow movable; it is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the joint to connect the bones, though muscles may still be needed to move them.

effect: The joint makes the elbow movable, and the new goal calls for muscles to pull in both directions.
reaction: The explanation clearly distinguishes joint movement from the force needed to produce it.
reason: I'll add the bending muscles to fill one of the arm's two pull slots.
expectation: I expect the bending muscles to fill the pull-to-bend slot, leaving the straightening slot empty.

alternatives.reason: The straightening muscles should fill the other slot, but either direction seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The bending muscles pull through tendons when they shorten, so the arm still needs a separate pull to straighten.
reaction: The tendon explanation makes the pulling mechanism clearer.
reason: The straightening muscles fill the remaining pull slot, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the straightening muscles to attach and give the arm a pull in the opposite direction.

effect: The straightening muscles complete the opposing pulls, showing how the arm can bend, straighten and hold its position.
reaction: The parallel explanation reinforces the idea, though repeating the tendon definition felt unnecessary.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the bending muscles was most worthwhile because the result explained how shortening muscle pulls bone through a tendon and why relaxing cannot push it back.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the straightening muscles repeated the tendon definition, although it usefully showed the opposite pull.

surprise.text: The explanation that relaxing a muscle cannot push the bones back clarified why a separate muscle group is needed.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: each part had a clear role in making or moving the elbow.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the opening made me curious about how the body supplies and directs the arm, although the choices so far were mostly straightforward.
